sources.title: Fragments Of Memories — BLACK/MATRIX 00 プレイ日記
sources.notes: PRIMARY JAPANESE SET A. Directly inspectable 2005 43-entry play diary spanning first clear and later-playthrough/endgame entries. It independently establishes the chronological story/battle flow and observed bonus placement. Newly indexed in this pass: BS2 and BS3 occur during chapter 3; BS4 occurs in chapter 4; BS5 `うちの子2` and BS6 `手合わせ` fire back-to-back in one chapter-4 free-action segment before mandatory progression resumes toward ラムシュタイン大聖堂; BS7/8 occur in chapter 5; BS9 in chapter 6; BS10 then BS11 in chapter 7; BS12 in chapter 8; and BS14 in chapter 9, where `セングラー` is visibly consumed during the added event. Use this as the independent contemporary chronology lane. Exact trigger chains that the diary does not print still require Set B or remain unsupported.

sources.title: PS～Black/Matrix00徹底攻略+極道研究
sources.notes: SUPPLEMENTAL CHINESE / ENGLISH-REFERENCE LANE ONLY. Directly inspectable detailed full walkthrough. The page author, DARKGUARD, explicitly says the guide was written from his own experience and completed after roughly one month of work; this is therefore an original Chinese walkthrough, NOT the vanished Japanese site later preserved by TSST. It provides chronological battle-stage order, free-action windows, hidden-shop/key-item notes, conditional battle rewards, ending-affecting conditions, and first-clear/NG+ information. Relevant unresolved-trigger material is already captured here: BS2 after 3-1 uses notebook `うちの子` then ダリア; BS3 uses the inn middle-aged man, フライ/プラン, the new notebook entry, then エクサル before optional battle `?1 問答無用`; BS5 uses notebook `うちの子で...` then the waiter; BS6 explicitly lists three Cipher Punk members (young man, woman, man), then notebook `いつものと...`, then ステイエン; BS10 explicitly uses シリア→ウェイトレス→プラン→片翼の天使→ウンダ長老→notebook `記憶を消...`→フライ→`う～ん...`; BS14 says BS4+BS7+BS10 cause notebook `カイン様`, then waiter, then `?4 クッタにトドメを`, whose reward is `絶望の光彩`. The BS6 young-member detail conflicts with derivative TSST (male+female only), and the explicit BS10 waitress placement sharpens TSST's uncertain waiter note, so Japanese corroboration is still required before those progression-critical facts can close the gate. Useful future `enGuide` detail also includes preparing before BS3's strong optional battle, the chapter-4 4-2 optional boss reward (`過酷な抱擁` + `募る思いの告白`), and late chapter-4 Painkiller/AoE cautions. Translate only relevant meaning into concise English. Never count this source as Set A/B and never use it to fill `jpGuide1`/`jpGuide2` or bypass missing Japanese verification.

disagreements: Research checkpoint after targeted Set-B pass. The route order remains established and must not be redesigned: Set A's 2005 diary independently anchors BS2/3 in chapter 3, BS5+6 together in one chapter-4 free-action segment, BS10 before BS11 in chapter 7, and BS14 in chapter 9 with `セングラー` consumed during the event. BS1 remains corrected to chapter 2 / 自由行動2. Set B directly covers chapter 2, chapter 5, chapter 8, endings/NG+, battle order, and BS11 corroboration. New clean Japanese Set-B evidence from BLACK/MATRIX総合スレッド Chapter:15 posts 319-321 closes only the BS14 item-condition sub-gap: `セングラー` is required for the chapter-9 クッタ-related event and must be held, not equipped. The gate is still OPEN. Remaining clean Japanese Set-B gaps: (1) exact trigger/timing facts for BS2/3; (2) exact trigger actions for grouped BS5/6; (3) exact trigger actions/timing for BS10; and (4) for BS14, the full BS4+BS7+BS10 prerequisite chain plus the exact `雑記帳（カイン様）→ウェイター` trigger. Supplemental evidence must not be promoted: TSST is derivative, and Chinese FFSKY is English-reference-only. Two supplemental discrepancies make direct Japanese verification especially important: FFSKY's BS6 sequence explicitly includes the young Cipher Punk member in addition to the woman/man while TSST lists only man+woman; FFSKY's BS10 sequence explicitly inserts the waitress after シリア while TSST only has an uncertain waiter note. FC2 indexed snippets continue to expose useful-looking chapter-4/7/9 lines but the underlying pages still return 403, so snippets remain search leads only. The release-era `BLACK/MATRIX 00攻略スレ２` thread id 1086009241 is independently confirmed by later Japanese threads, and those threads also name `BLUE MATRIX` as an攻略 lead, but neither source's relevant contents were recoverable directly in this pass. The official 175-page Japanese guide is confirmed to cover bonus stages, but no inspectable interior pages were recovered. Do not generate route_*.json until these progression-critical trigger gaps are closed by directly inspected independent Japanese evidence. Source-role lock added: FFSKY is confirmed from its own page as an original Chinese walkthrough (the author says he wrote it from his own experience over about a month), while TSST is the Japanese page that explicitly preserves notes from an older vanished site. Exact Japanese phrase searches for the unresolved trigger strings (`うちの子ですがね`, `いつものところ`, `記憶を消してくれ`, `カイン様` + waiter context) currently surface TSST but no new directly inspectable independent Japanese walkthrough. Future passes should therefore stop broad mirror rediscovery and only promote a new source when a concrete directly inspected Japanese page/scan/post closes one of the four listed gaps. Archive recovery status is now pinned: the original 2004 `BLACK/MATRIX 00攻略スレ２` URL is `game9.2ch.net/test/read.cgi/gameover/1086009241/` (the `gameover` board, not `gamesrpg`). Direct/native old-2ch archive variants plus discoverable Mimizun/Logsoku/Unkar/2ch.live/ruku/makimo/Wayback-style recovery paths did not produce directly inspectable thread content here; exact-ID and trigger-string searches also produced no recovered copy. A working later-thread mirror family (`famicom.doorblog.jp`) was checked specifically and did not surface the攻略 thread or missing trigger text. Exact bonus-scenario-title searches (`うちの子2`, `手合わせ`, `僕らの撲殺寸前事件・温泉編`, `血塗られたラブレター`) still collapse to derivative TSST or firsthand pages that mention completion without publishing the trigger chains.
